required_stages.description: Allocate a working buffer of M = next power of two >= N elements in data's dtype inside run().
One kernel pass copying data[0:N] into work[0:N] and filling work[N:M] with +inf (may be fused into the first stage group).

The bitonic schedule k = 2..M ascending, j = k/2..1 descending; per stage, partner i XOR j, direction (i AND k) == 0, strict-comparison swap performed once per pair by a single owner (lower-index lane is natural), in place in work; stages separated by global synchronisation unless confined to one program's slice.
Return work[:N] as a zero-copy view.

forbidden_substitutions.message: A library sort replaces the whole computation.
A DSL-level sort primitive replaces explicit compare-exchange stages; check that the network semantics and stage structure are preserved.
The pad must be a kernel pass over the run-allocated buffer, not host-side fill/copy operations.
clone() is only acceptable on the N <= 1 early-exit path.
Possible non-strict comparison in the swap test; equal values must never be exchanged (ignore if used only for bounds masks).
A second buffer suggests ping-pong buffering; the network must run in place in a single working buffer.
No dtype conversion is part of this operator.

required_evidence.message: No XOR partner computation found; partner = i XOR j is required.
No (i AND k) direction test found.
No select/where found for the compare-exchange.

outputs.aliasing: view of the run-allocated working buffer (length M = next power of two >= N), i.e. work[:N]; must never share storage with data

timing_boundary.notes: Measured: GPU time of all device work run() causes (the pad pass and every network stage); the M-element allocation call and the zero-copy slice are host work, not GPU time. Nothing is cached across calls; the metric counts only 2*N*dtype_size bytes while the executed work is the pad plus L(L+1)/2 in-place passes over M elements.
